body.heading: A big open mouth
paragraphs: A yawn is a slow, wide opening of the mouth with a deep breath in. It lasts about six seconds, and it is very hard to stop once it starts.
People yawn when they are tired or bored, but scientists say that is not the whole story. Even babies yawn before they are born.

body.heading: The cooling idea
paragraphs: One idea is that yawning helps cool the brain. The big breath brings in cooler air, and the stretch helps blood flow around the head.
A cool brain works better. So a yawn might be your brain's way of waking itself up and staying alert.

body.heading: Catchy yawns
paragraphs: Yawns are catching. Seeing someone yawn, hearing a yawn, or even reading about yawns can start one. You might be yawning right now.
Catching yawns seems to be linked to caring about others. Dogs can even catch yawns from their owners.

takeaway: Yawning may help cool the brain and wake it up, and yawns spread from person to person like a friendly echo.
